question:
In the following sentences, explain the antecedent of the pronoun (which thing the pronoun refers to), or state that it is ambiguous.
Sentence: The lawyer looked into illegal accusations against the cashier, because she needed to understand the case.
Options:
(A) The lawyer needed to understand
(B) The cashier needed to understand
(C) Ambiguous

segments.text: We need to determine antecedent of pronoun "she" in sentence: "The lawyer looked into illegal accusations against the cashier, because she needed to understand the case." Who is "she"?
The lawyer is a person, presumably female?
The pronoun "she" could refer to either.

The sentence structure: "The lawyer looked into illegal accusations against the cashier, because she needed to understand the case." The pronoun "she" is after a comma, referring to the subject of the clause "The lawyer looked into illegal accusations against the cashier".
Usually pronoun refers to the nearest preceding noun that matches gender.
The lawyer is the subject of the main clause.
The cashier is object of preposition "against".
The pronoun "she" likely refers to the lawyer.
In many contexts, pronoun refers to the subject of the clause.
The cashier could also be female.
But the pronoun is after a comma, not a relative clause.
Usually pronoun refers to the subject.
